subject: Changing to block updater throws errors or crashes R

messages.author: f66907f526d3c7bf
messages.subject: Changing to block updater throws errors or crashes R
parts:
I'm trying to get a GLLVM running in Nimble, without having had a lot of Nimble experience. I want to use a block updater for some of the nodes, to improve mixing. But I'm running into problems, no doubt due to me not understanding what I am doing.

The full code is here: <https://rpubs.com/oharar/HelpHelpNimble>, but I can't guarantee what it will give you.

The short version is that if I run the code below, I get the following warning messages, repeatedly:

Warning: after completing nimArr_2_ManyModelAccess, nimCurrent != nimEnd. Perhaps the NimArr was longer than the accessor?
Warning: in nimArr_2_ManyModelAccess, accessor larger than NimArr!
Warning: after completing ManyModelAccess_2_nimArr, nimCurrent != nimEnd. Perhaps the NimArr was longer than the accessor?

If I compile the document (or do other things that aren't repeatable), the R session just crashes. Can anyone help? I assume I'm just doing something dumb.


HeirOrd2D <- nimbleModel(HeirModel2D,
                      constants = OrdConsts,
                      data      = OrdData,
                      inits     = OrdInits2D(OrdData, 2))
HeirOrd2D.Comp <- compileNimble(HeirOrd2D)
HeirOrd2D.Conf <- configureMCMC(HeirOrd2D.Comp, monitors=ToMonitor)

HeirOrd2D.Conf$removeSamplers(c('alSpeciesSTAR', 'alSiteSTAR', 'L_v_STAR', 'lamSpSTAR'))

HeirOrd2D.Conf$addSampler(target =
                            c('alSpeciesSTAR', 'alSiteSTAR', 'L_v_STAR', 'lamSpSTAR'),
                          type = "RW_block")
# If I block these separately, runMCMC() crashes the R session
# HierOrd2D.Conf$addSampler(target = 'alSpeciesSTAR', type = "RW_block")
# HierOrd2D.Conf$addSampler(target = 'alSiteSTAR', type = "RW_block")
# HierOrd2D.Conf$addSampler(target = 'L_v_STAR', type = "RW_block")
# HierOrd2D.Conf$addSampler(target = 'lamSpSTAR', type = "RW_block")
HeirOrd2D.MCMC <- buildMCMC(HeirOrd2D.Conf)

HeirOrd2D.CompMCMC <- compileNimble(HeirOrd2D.MCMC)
HeirOrd2D.samp <- runMCMC(HeirOrd2D.CompMCMC,
                          nchains = 2, niter = 2e2, nburnin = 1e2, thin =1,
                          summary = TRUE, WAIC = FALSE)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Changing to block updater throws errors or crashes R
parts:
Hi Bob,

This looks really interesting.  Thanks for posting the question and giving clear code.

Your data setup code gave me an error at:
TraitData <- ConvData(TraitData.tmp, whNum = ToNum)

After some inspection, I did this, I think without harm, to keep moving:
TraitData.tmp <- TraitData.tmp[,-1]

The problem causing those error messages (and crashes) is something we should be error-trapping.  It's an easy mistake for a user to make, and the error information was inscrutable.  It looks like your inits value for alSpeciesSTAR should be length 68 but was length 74. If I am not lost, I think this was from using nrow(dat$Abund) instead of ncol(dat$Abund) in the last step of OrdInits2D.  Having the wrong length inits for alSpeciesSTAR caused a cascade of issues into the block sampler for alSpeciesSTAR (or the one with it as a component).

Another minor issue is that when you compile the model first and the MCMC second, you should include "project = model".  In your code:
HeirOrd2D.CompMCMC <- compileNimble(HeirOrd2D.MCMC, project = HeirOrd2D)

By the way, block samplers in many dimensions may not work well.  There is a control list parameter "tries", which I also noticed recently was left out of help(samplers), that will repeat the propose-accept-reject steps "tries" times, giving more effort into making a move among the many dimensions.  Otherwise the one sampler can often fail to make a move (a rejected proposal in Metropolis-Hastings) and then the entire block doesn't mix at all in that MCMC iteration.  Increasing tries doesn't fully alleviate the reasons that high-dimensional block sampling can struggle, but it can help.  It looks like this model presents a challenge in how to sample it well.

To increase tries, you would do 
HeirOrd2D.Conf$addSampler(target = 'alSpeciesSTAR', type = "RW_block", control = list(tries = 10)) # e.g. 10

Thanks again for the reproducible code.  That was extremely helpful.  I'll file an issue for us to error-trap the internals of how this happened.  It's a little surprising it hasn't manifested like this before.

-Perry

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Changing to block updater throws errors or crashes R
parts:
Quresh, briefly, I think you identified the issue, and I don't believe you can use the variable name "n.Xdelta" in your indexing of vector-valued nodes in calls to addSampler() or removeSamplers().  I think you'll need instead (if n.Xdelta=10, for example):

modelConf$removeSamplers(c("delta0", "deltaVec[1:10]"))

or, in the case that the *entirety* of "deltaVec" is in fact deltaVec[1:n.Xdelta], then you should be safe with:

modelConf$removeSamplers(c("delta0", "deltaVec"))

Could you give this a try, and let me know if this work?

Cheers,
Daniel

or, in the case that the *entirety* of "deltaVec" is in fact deltaVec[1:n.Xdelta], then you should be safe with:

 

modelConf$removeSamplers(c("delta0", "deltaVec"))

 

Could you give this a try, and let me know if this work?

 

Cheers,

Daniel

Hi. I am also getting this error. Based on the info here, it sounds like I might need to double check my initial values to make sure they have the correct dimensions, but before I do that, I wanted to make sure my coding is valid. I am doing this:

      model <- nimbleModel(code = model, name = "model",
                           constants = constants, data = data,
                           inits = init)
      Cmodel <- compileNimble(model)
      modelConf <- configureMCMC(model, thin = nt)
      modelConf$removeSamplers(c("delta0", "deltaVec[1:n.Xdelta]"))
      modelConf$addSampler(c("delta0", "deltaVec[1:n.Xdelta]"), type = "RW_block")
      modelConf$addMonitors(parameters)
      modelMCMC <- buildMCMC(modelConf)
      CmodelMCMC <- compileNimble(modelMCMC, project = model)
      CmodelMCMC$run(ni, reset = FALSE)
      return(as.mcmc(as.matrix(CmodelMCMC$mvSamples)))

 

'n.Xdelta' is listed in 'constants'. Is it valid to use a constant to define the indexing of nodes for adding and removing samplers, or do I have to do that differently?
On Friday, November 5, 2021 at 3:46:59 AM UTC-6 rni...@gmail.com wrote:

Thanks - that works. And thanks for the tip about the tries. I need to think about the blocking strategy. It's deliberately unidentifiable, so large blocks might actually help.

On Thursday, 4 November 2021 at 01:31:58 UTC+1 pdevalpine wrote:

Hi Bob,

 

This looks really interesting.  Thanks for posting the question and giving clear code.

 

Your data setup code gave me an error at:

TraitData <- ConvData(TraitData.tmp, whNum = ToNum)

 

After some inspection, I did this, I think without harm, to keep moving:

TraitData.tmp <- TraitData.tmp[,-1]

 

The problem causing those error messages (and crashes) is something we should be error-trapping.  It's an easy mistake for a user to make, and the error information was inscrutable.  It looks like your inits value for alSpeciesSTAR should be length 68 but was length 74. If I am not lost, I think this was from using nrow(dat$Abund) instead of ncol(dat$Abund) in the last step of OrdInits2D.  Having the wrong length inits for alSpeciesSTAR caused a cascade of issues into the block sampler for alSpeciesSTAR (or the one with it as a component).

 

Another minor issue is that when you compile the model first and the MCMC second, you should include "project = model".  In your code:

HeirOrd2D.CompMCMC <- compileNimble(HeirOrd2D.MCMC, project = HeirOrd2D)

 

By the way, block samplers in many dimensions may not work well.  There is a control list parameter "tries", which I also noticed recently was left out of help(samplers), that will repeat the propose-accept-reject steps "tries" times, giving more effort into making a move among the many dimensions.  Otherwise the one sampler can often fail to make a move (a rejected proposal in Metropolis-Hastings) and then the entire block doesn't mix at all in that MCMC iteration.  Increasing tries doesn't fully alleviate the reasons that high-dimensional block sampling can struggle, but it can help.  It looks like this model presents a challenge in how to sample it well.

 

To increase tries, you would do 

HeirOrd2D.Conf$addSampler(target = 'alSpeciesSTAR', type = "RW_block", control = list(tries = 10)) # e.g. 10

 

Thanks again for the reproducible code.  That was extremely helpful.  I'll file an issue for us to error-trap the internals of how this happened.  It's a little surprising it hasn't manifested like this before.

 

-Perry
